title: Run V3/V3_ifx and V4 ifx_profile parallel parity
goal: Execute an independent fail-closed parity comparison on the certified IFX commit and frozen 52-case production corpus without entering P10.3.
acceptanceCriteria: The accepted C6e-R1 decision, certified commit, V3/V3_ifx inventory, V4 receipt, package, Profile, Bundle and corpus hashes match the frozen identities.
The corpus contains ten clean, ten missing-input, ten zero-match and twenty-two blocking-claim violation cases with immutable fixture and input bindings.

V3/V3_ifx and V4 execute independently and the comparison records verdict, exit category, finding identity, subject semantics, evidence kind, detector, coverage, prerequisites, authority hashes and provenance.
The independent matrix contains no unresolved weakening, missing claim, accepted missing evidence, V4 zero-match success, stale evidence or unexplained verdict difference.
Protected authorities, installations, corpus inputs and Target roots remain byte-invariant.
P10.3, activation, publication, V3 retirement and IFX cutover remain outside scope.
risks: A corpus or authority identity drift would merge evidence from different version-ledger tuples.
A candidate-owned comparison could allow V4 to judge itself.
A semantic mapping could hide a weaker severity, accepted missing evidence or zero-match success.
P10.2 completion could be misrepresented as P10.3 activation or V3 retirement authority.
decisions: Use the exact certified C6c production-module case projection rather than inventing a second unbound corpus.
Run engines in separate mutable roots and run comparison only after both result sets close.
Treat unexplained differences as blocking and retain stopped evidence without in-place repair or rerun.
